items.text: Oil prices have surged sharply: WTI +9.6% and Brent +8.8% since Sept 1, reflecting geopolitical tensions (US-Iran escalation in early September) and Middle East supply risks. For high-yield and distressed credits in energy, refining, and shipping, this creates both upside (energy company revenues) and downside (elevated cost inflation for transport-heavy issuers). Tighter 2-year spreads and falling term premiums may pressure valuations in this volatility regime.

Jobless claims edged up to 206K (from 204K), and average hourly earnings decelerated to 3.09% YoY from 3.24%, signaling early softness in wage pressure. However, payroll growth remains robust at 162K. This mixed signal complicates the Fed's path: slower wage growth supports another rate cut, but solid employment argues for patience. Tightening labor market access may pressure issuers reliant on cost discipline.

Core CPI eased to 2.47% YoY (vs 2.57%) and headline PPI fell sharply to 4.66% from 5.54%, but headline CPI ticked up slightly to 3.3%. Sticky core services inflation (via PCE core at 3.34% unchanged month-to-month) remains the Fed's headache. For credit investors, sticky core inflation keeps real rates elevated and widens the path for defaults in rate-sensitive or heavily leveraged sectors.

The Fed held rates flat at 3.75% through early September. The 10Y yield rose to 4.77% from 4.73%, and the 2-10 curve steepened slightly to 41bps. The ECB remains at 2.25% deposit rate (June hike to 2.25%) with mixed signals on further moves. Persistent term premiums and higher real rates support credit compression but increase refinancing pressure on floating-rate or near-maturity credit.

Credit spreads are mixed: HY OAS tightened slightly to 2.65% from 2.63%, while IG OAS widened to 0.81% from 0.80% (unusual inversion signals caution among IG investors). CCC OAS gapped wider to 10.51% from 10.42%, reflecting distress-sector volatility. VIX at 14.32 (mild compression) masks underlying dispersion; watch for credit market fragmentation as earnings season nears.

ISM Services PMI stood at 54.0 in June, keeping the index in expansion territory for a 24th consecutive month, but the August ISM Manufacturing fell to 54.6 from 55.6. GDPNow jumped to 4.75% (from 1.54% in July), driven by inventory and trade surprises, but this may not persist. Consumer spending (retail +5.75% YoY ex-autos) remains resilient despite weak sentiment, though savings rate stayed flat at 3%. Growth appears late-cycle and subject to policy/earnings revisions.

The University of Michigan's consumer sentiment index fell to 51 in early August 2026, down from 55.2 in July and below market expectations of 54.5, as fuel and food costs spiked. July 2026 retail sales (total) fell 0.6% MoM but rose 5.0% YoY, showing uneven consumer health. Housing remains soft: mortgage rates at 6.71% and housing starts fell to 1,239K from 1,415K. Distressed consumer-facing credit (autos, retail, mortgage servicers) faces headwinds from sentiment, rates, and demand pullback.

themeCards.title: Middle East Energy Shock
themeCards.statusLine: US-Iran escalation in early September drove oil +10% in days; WTI at 91.48, Brent at 96.02. Risks of sustained supply disruption or further strikes remain elevated, particularly via Strait of Hormuz chokepoint.
themeCards.relevance: For special situations credit: direct upside in energy & shipping, but significant tail risk to leverage ratios, capex budgets, and hedging costs across transport, chemicals, utilities, and cyclical industrials. Volatility may create tactical entry points in distressed energy credit if spreads fail to widen meaningfully.

themeCards.title: Fed Rate Cuts Delayed; Sticky Core Inflation
themeCards.statusLine: Core PCE/services inflation remains at 3.34%, well above the 2% target. Fed on hold at 3.75%; market no longer pricing imminent cuts despite softer wage data. Curve flattening and real rate persistence press valuations.
themeCards.relevance: High-yield and distressed credit heavily exposed to leverage multiples and refinancing windows. Delay in cuts extends pressure on floating-rate issuers and those with near-term maturities. Widens basis between IG and HY; watch for credit market stress if earnings disappoints into Q3/Q4.

themeCards.title: China Structural Slowdown; Export Orders Fragile
themeCards.statusLine: China manufacturing PMI at 49.8 (sub-50 contraction for 2nd straight month); services at 49.0. Output and new orders improved but employment remains weak and small firms still contracting. Non-manufacturing slack is drag on capex and investment.
themeCards.relevance: Matters for special situations: global supply chain stress, commodity crash risk (iron ore, copper), and spillover to EM credit and export-oriented credits in APAC. Also pressures US multinationals and leveraged China-exposed LBOs. Potential entry point if contagion fears prove overblown and policy stimulus gains traction.

themeCards.title: Consumer Sentiment Cliff; Tariff & Geopolitical Fear
themeCards.statusLine: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index fell to 51.7 in August, a 6.3% decrease from July. Consumers expect 4% inflation YoY; anxiety over Iran war, tariffs, and gas prices has reversed two months of gains. Sentiment now historically depressed.
themeCards.relevance: Special situations opportunity: consumer-facing credit (retail, autos, restaurants) at risk if sentiment-driven spending reversal accelerates. Negative wealth effects from stock market volatility and gas price spikes could trigger defaults in auto finance, credit cards, and levered retailers. Watch for covenant waivers and forbearance requests.

themeCards.title: IG/HY Spread Inversion; Sector Bifurcation
themeCards.statusLine: IG OAS widened to 0.81 from 0.80; HY OAS tightened to 2.65 from 2.63 — unusual inversion. CCC OAS blown out to 10.51 from 10.42, signaling distress-cohort stress. Dispersion rising as mega-cap tech, AI beneficiaries, and defensives de-rate vs. cyclicals and rate-sensitives.
themeCards.relevance: Classic late-cycle credit divergence. Distressed and high-beta credits (retail, autos, regional banks, small-cap industrials) likely to underperform. Special situations investors should scan for (i) forced selling in passive/index products, (ii) covenant pressure in CCC-rated issuers, and (iii) M&A rescue scenarios in mid-market.

themeCards.title: Housing Correction & Mortgage Rate Lock
themeCards.statusLine: Housing starts fell to 1,239K from 1,415K; existing home sales at 4.06M (down from 4.13M). Mortgage rates at 6.71% (up from 6.66%) are creating affordability wall and demand destruction. Builder confidence likely declining.
themeCards.relevance: Special situations angles: (i) homebuilder credit facing margin compression and inventory writedowns; (ii) mortgage servicers and mortgage REIT stress if delinquency/forbearance rises; (iii) construction credit (equipment rental, materials) at risk; (iv) potential CRE spillover if residential yields don't adjust and development stops.

chinaPMI.delta: official manufacturing PMI, still in contraction but beat 49.7 consensus in August

ismServices.delta: September 3 actual beat 54.1 consensus; prior July was 54.1

existingHome.delta: July 2026, down from June 4.13M, softer housing demand

consensus.PCE: 3.6% YoY headline, 3.2% core exp (September release later month)
consensus.GDP: No consensus yet; prior Q2 was 1.5%, GDPNow tracking 4.75% for Q3

regime.label: Late-cycle transition
regime.detail: Fed on hold, term premiums sticky, oil shock, consumer sentiment cliff, HY/IG bifurcation, growth decelerating but resilient. Refinancing pressure mounting; distressed cohort emerging.
